Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) Poverty of expression in face happens in........?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Poverty of facial expression (hypomimia) is a classic feature of Parkinsonism. It results from bradykinesia and reduced spontaneous facial movements, giving the characteristic “masked face” appearance. Other typical features include resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability. Myasthenia gravis can cause facial weakness and fatigability, but “poverty of expression” is classically associated with Parkinsonism. Marasmus and kwashiorkor may cause characteristic nutritional appearances but do not classically produce hypomimia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Parkinsonism → masked face / hypomimia

  • Bradykinesia → reduced spontaneous movements

  • Other features → resting tremor + rigidity

  • Myasthenia gravis → fatigable weakness, ptosis, diplopia

Exam Pearl:
Poverty of facial expression = masked facies → Parkinsonism.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Tubular membrane is maximum permeable to which of the following?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the given substances, the renal tubular membrane is most permeable to urea. Urea is freely filtered at the glomerulus and is also reabsorbed from the renal tubules, particularly in the inner medullary collecting duct, where its permeability increases under the influence of ADH. This contributes to the medullary osmotic gradient and urine concentration.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Urea → highly permeable through parts of renal tubules

  • Inulin → freely filtered, not reabsorbed

  • Creatinine → filtered, with minimal tubular secretion and essentially no reabsorption

  • Sucrose → filtered but not significantly reabsorbed

  • ADH → increases urea permeability in the inner medullary collecting duct

Exam Pearl:
Among these options, urea has the greatest tubular reabsorption/permeability.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) Fever with drenching night sweat occurs in........?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the given substances, the renal tubular membrane is most permeable to urea. Urea is freely filtered at the glomerulus and is also reabsorbed from the renal tubules, particularly in the inner medullary collecting duct, where its permeability increases under the influence of ADH. This contributes to the medullary osmotic gradient and urine concentration.

  • Urea → highly permeable through parts of renal tubules

  • Inulin → freely filtered, not reabsorbed

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) Maximum absorption of bile occurs at….?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Most bile salts are reabsorbed in the terminal ileum by active transport and returned to the liver through the portal circulation. This recycling process is called the enterohepatic circulation. Although some bile salts can be absorbed passively in the proximal small intestine, the majority (about 95%) are recovered in the terminal ileum. The colon is not the major site of bile salt absorption.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bile salts → terminal ileum

  • ~95% → reabsorbed

  • Process → enterohepatic circulation

  • Ileal disease/resection → bile salt loss → bile acid diarrhea

  • Remaining bile salts → fecal excretion

Exam Pearl:
Maximum bile salt absorption = terminal ileum.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) Productive cough with frothy sputum occurs in........?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Frothy sputum, particularly pink or blood-tinged frothy sputum, is a classic feature of acute pulmonary edema. Increased hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary capillaries causes fluid to move into the alveoli. Mixing of this fluid with air and surfactant produces frothy sputum, while small amounts of RBC leakage can give it a pink color. Asthma typically causes scanty, mucoid sputum; COPD commonly produces mucoid or purulent sputum; and TB may cause blood-streaked sputum or hemoptysis rather than characteristic frothy sputum.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pink frothy sputum → acute pulmonary edema

  • Pulmonary edema → ↑ pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure

  • Asthma → mucoid sputum

  • COPD → mucoid/purulent sputum

  • TB → hemoptysis may occur

Exam Pearl:
Pink frothy sputum = pulmonary edema until proven otherwise.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) Cheyne stokes breathing is not seen in….?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cheyne–Stokes breathing is a periodic breathing pattern characterized by progressive increase and then decrease in tidal volume followed by a period of apnea. It is classically associated with congestive heart failure, severe brain damage, and can occur in uremia. It is not a typical feature of bronchial asthma, where the main respiratory abnormality is episodic airflow obstruction with wheezing, prolonged expiration, and dyspnea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cheyne–Stokes → crescendo–decrescendo breathing + apnea

  • Seen in → heart failure

  • Seen in → brain/CNS damage

  • Can occur in → uremia

  • Not typical → bronchial asthma

Exam Pearl:
Cheyne–Stokes breathing = heart failure/CNS disease, not asthma.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Weight loss is not found in....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypopituitarism is generally associated with weight gain rather than weight loss, particularly when there is secondary hypothyroidism and/or hypogonadism. In contrast, Type 1 diabetes mellitus causes weight loss due to insulin deficiency and increased catabolism, while thyrotoxicosis causes weight loss because of increased basal metabolic rate and energy expenditure. Hypogonadism can also be associated with changes in body composition, but the classic endocrine causes of weight loss among these options are T1DM and thyrotoxicosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type 1 DM → weight loss

  • Thyrotoxicosis → weight loss

  • Hypopituitarism → weight gain is more typical

  • Hyperthyroidism → ↑ metabolic rate → weight loss

Exam Pearl:
Weight loss + polyuria/polydipsia → think Type 1 DM; weight loss + tremor/palpitations → think thyrotoxicosis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) ST elevation in ECG signifies myocardial.....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
ST-segment elevation classically signifies acute myocardial injury, particularly transmural myocardial injury. In acute coronary syndrome, ST elevation may indicate an acute coronary occlusion and is characteristic of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, the ECG terminology distinguishes the three patterns: T-wave changes → ischemia, ST-segment changes → injury, and pathological Q waves → infarction/necrosis. Therefore, among the given options, myocardial injury is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T-wave inversion → ischemia

  • ST elevation/depression → myocardial injury

  • Pathological Q wave → infarction/necrosis

  • ST elevation + compatible clinical picture → consider STEMI

Exam Pearl:
ST elevation = myocardial injury.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) Disadvantages of Furosemide excludes...?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Furosemide, a loop diuretic, inhibits the Na⁺-K⁺-2Cl⁻ cotransporter (NKCC2) in the thick ascending limb. Its adverse effects include hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, and hypocalcaemia due to increased urinary electrolyte loss. It also decreases uric acid excretion, causing hyperuricaemia, which may precipitate gout. Therefore, hypouricaemia is not a disadvantage of furosemide.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Furosemide → hypokalaemia

  • → hypomagnesaemia

  • → hypocalcaemia

  • → hyperuricaemia (not hypouricaemia)

  • Mechanism → blocks NKCC2 in thick ascending limb

Exam Pearl:
Loop diuretics waste Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ and increase uric acid → “loops lose calcium.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Immediate percutaneous needle aspiration is done in...... Intercostal space anteriorly in mid clavicular line?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
For immediate needle decompression of a tension pneumothorax, the traditional landmark is the 2nd intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line. The needle is inserted just above the upper border of the rib to avoid the intercostal neurovascular bundle. Modern trauma guidelines may also favor the 4th/5th intercostal space at the anterior or mid-axillary line in many adults because of better success rates, but for this classic MCQ wording, 2nd ICS, mid-clavicular line is the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Classic needle decompression → 2nd ICS, mid-clavicular line

  • Insert just above the rib

  • Alternative modern site → 4th/5th ICS, anterior/mid-axillary line

  • Indication → tension pneumothorax

Exam Pearl:
Classic MCQ answer: 2nd intercostal space in the mid-clavicular line.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১১) Which investigation is more sensitive to diagnose bronchiectasis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest is the most sensitive and preferred imaging investigation for diagnosing bronchiectasis. It can directly demonstrate bronchial dilatation, lack of normal bronchial tapering, bronchial wall thickening, and the classic “signet-ring” sign. A chest X-ray may show indirect or nonspecific findings but can be normal in mild disease. Sputum examination is useful for identifying infecting organisms, while serum immunoglobulin testing helps investigate an underlying cause rather than directly diagnosing bronchiectasis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Best/sensitive investigation → HRCT chest

  • CXR → may be normal or nonspecific

  • Sputum → identifies causative organisms

  • Serum immunoglobulins → evaluate underlying etiology

  • HRCT → signet-ring sign

Exam Pearl:
Suspected bronchiectasis → HRCT chest is the investigation of choice.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Which of the following is not a feature of bacterial pneumonia?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bacterial pneumonia typically presents with an abrupt onset, fever, productive cough with purulent sputum, and clinical/radiological features of consolidation. Leukocytosis with neutrophilia is also common. A dry cough is more characteristic of atypical pneumonia, such as infections caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydophila pneumoniae, or respiratory viruses. Therefore, dry cough is the feature that is not typical of bacterial pneumonia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bacterial pneumonia → abrupt onset

  • → productive cough

  • → lobar consolidation

  • → neutrophilic leukocytosis

  • Atypical pneumonia → dry cough + diffuse/interstitial infiltrates

Exam Pearl:
Bacterial pneumonia = productive cough; atypical pneumonia = dry cough.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) Deficiency of which vitamin is a risk factor for Tuberculosis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Vitamin A deficiency is associated with an increased susceptibility to tuberculosis (TB) because vitamin A plays an important role in maintaining epithelial integrity and supporting immune function. Deficiency can impair host defense against infections, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Among the options, vitamin A is the best-established nutritional risk factor for TB.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Vitamin A deficiency → ↑ susceptibility to TB

  • Vitamin A → important for cell-mediated immunity

  • TB risk factors → malnutrition, diabetes, HIV, immunosuppression

  • Vitamin D also has an important role in antimycobacterial immunity

Exam Pearl:
Vitamin A deficiency → increased susceptibility to tuberculosis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Non metastatic neurological manifestation due to bronchial carcinoma excludes?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bronchial carcinoma can produce several non-metastatic (paraneoplastic) neurological syndromes. These include peripheral polyneuropathy, subacute cerebellar/cerebral degeneration, and Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS), which is particularly associated with small-cell lung carcinoma. Myelopathy is not a classic paraneoplastic neurological manifestation of bronchial carcinoma and is therefore the best answer for the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Small-cell lung carcinoma → Lambert–Eaton syndrome

  • Paraneoplastic → polyneuropathy

  • → subacute cerebellar degeneration

  • Myelopathy → not a typical paraneoplastic manifestation

Exam Pearl:
Bronchial carcinoma + proximal muscle weakness + autonomic symptoms → Lambert–Eaton syndrome.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) Passage of black, tarry stools containing altered blood is called....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Melaena (melena) refers to the passage of black, tarry, foul-smelling stools containing digested/altered blood, usually resulting from upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The blood is altered by digestive enzymes and intestinal bacteria as it passes through the gastrointestinal tract. Common causes include peptic ulcer disease, gastritis, and esophageal varices. Hematemesis means vomiting blood, hematochezia refers to passage of fresh or bright-red blood per rectum, and hemoptysis is coughing up blood from the respiratory tract.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Melaena → black, tarry stool

  • Usually → upper GI bleeding

  • Hematemesis → vomiting blood

  • Hematochezia → fresh blood per rectum

  • Hemoptysis → coughing up blood

Exam Pearl:
Black + tarry + foul-smelling stool = Melaena.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Which is not an inherited liver disease?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Budd–Chiari syndrome is not an inherited liver disease. It results from hepatic venous outflow obstruction, most commonly due to hepatic vein thrombosis, and is often associated with acquired hypercoagulable states such as myeloproliferative disorders. In contrast, Gilbert syndrome, Wilson disease, and hereditary hemochromatosis are inherited disorders. Gilbert syndrome causes mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, Wilson disease causes abnormal copper accumulation, and hemochromatosis causes excessive iron deposition in tissues.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Budd–Chiari → hepatic venous outflow obstruction

  • Gilbert syndrome → ↓ bilirubin conjugation

  • Wilson disease → copper accumulation

  • Hemochromatosis → iron accumulation

  • Gilbert, Wilson, hemochromatosis → inherited disorders

Exam Pearl:
Budd–Chiari = acquired hepatic venous outflow obstruction, not a hereditary liver disease.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) Which analgesic is usually chosen for acute pancreatitis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acute pancreatitis can cause severe upper abdominal pain, and opioid analgesics are commonly used when strong analgesia is required. Historically, morphine was avoided because of concern about sphincter of Oddi spasm, but current evidence does not support avoiding opioids for this reason. Opioids provide effective pain relief and are commonly used in moderate-to-severe acute pancreatitis. NSAIDs or non-opioid analgesics may be sufficient for mild pain, depending on the patient and clinical setting.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute pancreatitis → severe abdominal pain

  • Moderate/severe pain → opioid analgesics

  • Morphine is not contraindicated solely because of sphincter of Oddi concerns

  • NSAIDs/non-opioids → possible for mild pain

Exam Pearl:
Severe pain in acute pancreatitis → opioids are appropriate analgesics.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) Which is the gold standard but invasive & seldom used test of pancreatic function?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Collection of pure pancreatic juice after secretin injection
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The secretin stimulation test with direct collection of pancreatic juice is considered the gold standard for assessing exocrine pancreatic function, particularly pancreatic bicarbonate secretion. After IV secretin administration, pancreatic secretions are collected, usually via duodenal intubation, and analyzed for bicarbonate and enzyme output. It is invasive, technically demanding, and rarely used in routine practice. MRCP and ERCP primarily assess pancreatic ductal anatomy, while USG is mainly an imaging investigation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Exocrine pancreatic function → Secretin stimulation test

  • Gold standard → direct collection of pancreatic juice

  • Measures → bicarbonate + enzyme secretion

  • ERCP → ductal anatomy/intervention

  • MRCP → non-invasive ductal imaging

Exam Pearl:
Gold standard for pancreatic exocrine function = secretin stimulation with direct pancreatic juice collection.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) Which is not true about hepatocellular jaundice?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In hepatocellular jaundice, there is predominantly hepatocyte injury, so ALT and AST are markedly elevated. Prolonged PT may occur due to impaired synthesis of clotting factors by the liver and is an important marker of hepatic synthetic dysfunction. Although ALP can increase, a marked/disproportionate rise in ALP is more characteristic of cholestatic or obstructive jaundice. Therefore, among the options, high rise of ALP is not typical of hepatocellular jaundice.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hepatocellular → ↑↑ ALT/AST

  • Cholestatic/obstructive → ↑↑ ALP + GGT

  • Severe liver dysfunction → prolonged PT/INR

  • ALT is generally more liver-specific than AST

Exam Pearl:
Marked transaminase elevation → hepatocellular; marked ALP elevation → cholestatic.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Which is not a feature of pain of PUD?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pain due to peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is classically epigastric, often episodic, and has a characteristic relationship with meals. Duodenal ulcer pain may improve after eating and recur 2–5 hours later or at night, while gastric ulcer pain may worsen with food. Radiation to the back is not a typical feature of uncomplicated PUD and should raise suspicion for other conditions, particularly pancreatitis or a penetrating ulcer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PUD → epigastric pain

  • Usually → episodic

  • Gastric ulcer → pain may worsen with meals

  • Duodenal ulcer → pain may improve with meals, then recur later

  • Back radiation → think pancreatitis

Exam Pearl:
Epigastric pain radiating to the back = pancreatitis more than uncomplicated PUD.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) What is the most common cause of dysuria?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cystitis (urinary bladder infection) is the most common cause of dysuria, particularly in women. Dysuria refers to pain, burning, or discomfort during urination. Acute cystitis commonly presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, and suprapubic discomfort. Urethritis can also cause dysuria, particularly in sexually transmitted infections, while prostatitis is an important cause in men. Bladder outflow obstruction typically causes hesitancy, poor urinary stream, and incomplete emptying rather than being the most common cause of dysuria.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common cause of dysuria → cystitis

  • Cystitis → dysuria + frequency + urgency

  • Urethritis → consider STI

  • Prostatitis → dysuria + pelvic/perineal pain

  • Outflow obstruction → poor stream + hesitancy

Exam Pearl:
Dysuria + frequency + urgency = think cystitis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) Which is Benzodiazepine antagonist?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Flumazenil is a specific benzodiazepine receptor antagonist used to reverse the sedative effects of benzodiazepines. It acts competitively at the GABA-A receptor benzodiazepine binding site. However, it should be used cautiously because it can precipitate seizures and acute withdrawal, particularly in chronic benzodiazepine users or mixed overdoses involving pro-convulsant drugs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Benzodiazepine antagonist → Flumazenil

  • Opioid antagonist → Naloxone

  • Organophosphate poisoning → Atropine + pralidoxime

  • Paracetamol toxicity → N-acetylcysteine

Exam Pearl:
“Benzodiazepine → Flumazenil; Opioid → Naloxone.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) What is the sodium content of 1L NS?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Normal saline (0.9% NaCl) contains 154 mmol/L of sodium (Na⁺) and 154 mmol/L of chloride (Cl⁻), giving a total osmolarity of approximately 308 mOsm/L. It is called “normal” or “physiological” saline because its concentration is close to the osmotic concentration of plasma, although its chloride content is relatively high and large volumes can contribute to hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • 0.9% NS → Na⁺ = 154 mmol/L

  • Cl⁻ = 154 mmol/L

  • Total osmolarity ≈ 308 mOsm/L

  • Large-volume NS → risk of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis

Exam Pearl:
1 L of 0.9% NS contains 154 mmol sodium.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Which electrolyte imbalance causes muscle weakness?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypokalemia commonly causes muscle weakness, fatigue, cramps, and in severe cases, paralysis. Low extracellular potassium increases the resting membrane potential (makes it more negative), reducing muscle excitability. Severe hypokalemia can also cause cardiac arrhythmias and characteristic ECG changes such as flattened T waves, ST depression, and prominent U waves. Although hyperkalemia can also cause muscle weakness, the classic electrolyte imbalance associated with muscle weakness in this type of MCQ is hypokalemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypokalemia → muscle weakness + cramps

  • Severe hypokalemia → paralysis

  • ECG → U waves, ↓T-wave amplitude, ST depression

  • Hyperkalemia → muscle weakness + potentially dangerous arrhythmias

Exam Pearl:
Muscle weakness + U waves → think hypokalemia.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Which poisoning is common in children?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Kerosene poisoning is a common accidental poisoning in children, particularly due to ingestion from improperly stored household fuel. The major danger is aspiration into the lungs, which can cause chemical pneumonitis. Symptoms may include coughing, choking, vomiting, respiratory distress, and hypoxia. Children are especially vulnerable because kerosene is often stored in accessible containers and has a low viscosity, making aspiration more likely. Organophosphate poisoning is also important in agricultural settings, but kerosene ingestion is classically associated with accidental poisoning in children.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Children → Kerosene poisoning commonly occurs accidentally

  • Main complication → aspiration pneumonitis

  • Avoid inducing vomiting after hydrocarbon ingestion

  • Respiratory symptoms → monitor for chemical pneumonitis

Exam Pearl:
Child + accidental hydrocarbon ingestion → think kerosene poisoning.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) Which disease is diagnosed by water deprivation test?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The water deprivation test is used to evaluate patients with polyuria and polydipsia, particularly to diagnose and differentiate diabetes insipidus (DI) from primary polydipsia. During water deprivation, a normal person concentrates the urine. In diabetes insipidus, urine remains inappropriately dilute because of either ADH deficiency (central DI) or renal resistance to ADH (nephrogenic DI). Desmopressin is then used to help distinguish central from nephrogenic DI.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Water deprivation test → Diabetes insipidus

  • Central DI → responds to desmopressin

  • Nephrogenic DI → little/no response

  • Normal person → urine becomes concentrated

Exam Pearl:
Polyuria + dilute urine + water deprivation test → think Diabetes insipidus.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) Which microbe is most common cause of meningitis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Viruses are the most common overall cause of meningitis, particularly in children and young adults. Viral meningitis is often caused by enteroviruses, including coxsackieviruses and echoviruses. Pyogenic bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis are major causes of acute bacterial meningitis and are more severe, but they are not the most common cause of meningitis overall. Tuberculosis and fungal meningitis are less common and typically occur in specific risk groups.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common overall cause → Viruses

  • Common viral cause → Enteroviruses

  • Major bacterial causes → S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis

  • TB meningitis → usually subacute/chronic

  • Fungal meningitis → often immunocompromised patients

Exam Pearl:
Most common meningitis overall = viral meningitis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Somatic symptoms of panic disorder excludes....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Panic disorder commonly produces sudden episodes of intense fear accompanied by autonomic and somatic symptoms. Typical symptoms include palpitations, chest pain/discomfort, shortness of breath, dizziness, sweating, trembling, choking sensation, and paresthesia. Muscle tension is more characteristic of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) rather than panic disorder. Therefore, muscle tension is the best answer for the feature that is not typical of panic disorder.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Panic disorder → palpitations

  • → chest pain/discomfort

  • → paresthesia

  • → dyspnea, sweating, tremor, dizziness

  • Muscle tension → more typical of GAD

Exam Pearl:
Panic attack = sudden autonomic symptoms; muscle tension → think GAD.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Topical retinoids are used in.....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Topical retinoids such as tretinoin, adapalene, and tazarotene are commonly used in the treatment of acne vulgaris. They normalize follicular keratinization, prevent formation of microcomedones, and help reduce comedones and inflammatory lesions. They are particularly important as first-line topical therapy for comedonal acne. Retinoids may also be used in psoriasis (e.g., topical tazarotene), but among these options, acne is the classic and most common indication.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Topical retinoids → Acne vulgaris

  • Examples → Tretinoin, adapalene, tazarotene

  • Main action → comedolytic

  • Also useful → topical tazarotene in psoriasis

Exam Pearl:
Topical retinoids = first-line comedolytic treatment for acne.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) Which is the most common presentation of psoriasis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Plaque psoriasis (psoriasis vulgaris) is the most common clinical type of psoriasis, accounting for the majority of cases. It presents as well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered by silvery-white scales, commonly affecting the extensor surfaces such as the elbows and knees, as well as the scalp and lumbosacral region. Guttate, pustular, and erythrodermic psoriasis are less common variants.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common type → Plaque psoriasis

  • Also called → Psoriasis vulgaris

  • Lesions → well-demarcated erythematous plaques + silvery scales

  • Common sites → elbows, knees, scalp

  • Guttate → often follows streptococcal infection

Exam Pearl:
Most common psoriasis = chronic plaque (psoriasis vulgaris).

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Which is most common type of arthritis in world?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common type of arthritis worldwide. It is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone changes, osteophyte formation, and varying degrees of synovial inflammation. It commonly affects weight-bearing joints such as the knees and hips, as well as the hands and spine. Rheumatoid arthritis, gout, and other inflammatory arthritides are less common.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common arthritis worldwide → Osteoarthritis

  • Nature → degenerative

  • Common joints → knees, hips, hands, spine

  • Typical feature → osteophytes

  • RA → autoimmune inflammatory arthritis

Exam Pearl:
Most common arthritis = Osteoarthritis (OA).

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) Which is an increase in the size of cells resulting in increase in the size of the organ?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells, resulting in an increase in the size of the affected organ or tissue. It occurs mainly in tissues with limited ability to undergo cell division, such as cardiac and skeletal muscle. In contrast, hyperplasia is an increase in the number of cells, while atrophy is a decrease in cell size and/or number. Metaplasia is a reversible change from one differentiated cell type to another.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypertrophy → ↑ cell size

  • Hyperplasia → ↑ cell number

  • Atrophy → ↓ cell size/number

  • Metaplasia → one mature cell type → another

Exam Pearl:
Hypertrophy = bigger cells; Hyperplasia = more cells.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৩) Increased cytosolic calcium ion activates following enzymes except......?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
An increase in cytosolic Ca²⁺ is an important mechanism of cell injury. Excess intracellular calcium activates several enzymes, including phospholipases, proteases, and ATPases. Phospholipases damage cell membranes, proteases damage cytoskeletal and membrane proteins, and ATPases increase ATP consumption, worsening cellular energy depletion. Peroxidase is not classically listed among the enzymes activated by increased cytosolic Ca²⁺ in cellular injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ↑ Cytosolic Ca²⁺ → activates phospholipases

  • → activates proteases

  • → activates ATPases

  • → damages membranes, cytoskeleton, and mitochondria

  • Peroxidase → not a classic Ca²⁺-activated enzyme

Exam Pearl:
Cell injury + ↑ intracellular Ca²⁺ → phospholipase + protease + ATPase activation.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) Which is not a type of nuclear change in irreversible cell injury?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The three classic nuclear changes in irreversible cell injury/necrosis are pyknosis, karyorrhexis, and karyolysis. Pyknosis is nuclear shrinkage with increased basophilia, karyorrhexis is fragmentation of the pyknotic nucleus, and karyolysis is dissolution/fading of the nucleus due to DNase activity. Karyokinesis means nuclear division during mitosis, so it is not a nuclear change of irreversible cell injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pyknosis → nuclear shrinkage

  • Karyorrhexis → nuclear fragmentation

  • Karyolysis → nuclear dissolution

  • Karyokinesis → nuclear division (mitosis)

Exam Pearl:
Necrosis: Pyknosis → Karyorrhexis → Karyolysis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) Which one is the local factor that influence wound healing?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Infection is a local factor that significantly delays wound healing. Bacteria and their toxins can prolong inflammation, damage newly formed tissue, and interfere with collagen deposition and wound contraction. In contrast, protein deficiency, diabetes mellitus, and steroid therapy are considered systemic factors that impair wound healing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Local factor → Infection

  • Systemic factors → malnutrition/protein deficiency, diabetes, steroids

  • Infection → prolonged inflammation + delayed healing

  • Diabetes → impaired immunity + microvascular dysfunction

Exam Pearl:
Local factors: infection, poor blood supply, foreign body, mechanical stress.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) Which is not an example of autosomal dominant disorder?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Wilson disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene, leading to impaired copper excretion and copper accumulation in tissues. In contrast, Marfan syndrome, tuberous sclerosis, and achondroplasia are classically autosomal dominant disorders. Therefore, Wilson disease is the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Marfan syndrome → Autosomal dominant

  • Tuberous sclerosis → Autosomal dominant

  • Achondroplasia → Autosomal dominant

  • Wilson disease → Autosomal recessive

  • Wilson → ATP7B mutation + copper accumulation

Exam Pearl:
Wilson = AR; Marfan + Tuberous sclerosis + Achondroplasia = AD.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) Paget’s disease is precancerous lesion for--?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Paget disease of bone is a chronic disorder of bone remodeling characterized by excessive and disorganized bone turnover. However, an important clarification is that Paget disease of bone is not itself considered a classic precancerous lesion. It is associated with a small increased risk of developing osteosarcoma, a malignant bone tumor. Among the given options, bone is the intended answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Paget disease of bone → abnormal bone remodeling

  • Rare complication → osteosarcoma

  • Common sites → pelvis, femur, vertebrae, skull

  • Usually occurs in older adults

Exam Pearl:
Paget disease of bone → rare association with osteosarcoma.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) Anti tumor immune mechanism exclude--?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Major anti-tumor immune mechanisms include NK cells, macrophages, and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). NK cells can directly kill tumor cells, macrophages can destroy tumor cells after activation, and ADCC allows immune cells such as NK cells to kill antibody-coated tumor cells. Helper T lymphocytes (CD4⁺ T cells) mainly coordinate and enhance immune responses through cytokine secretion rather than directly acting as a primary tumor-killing mechanism. Therefore, among the options, helper T lymphocytes are the best answer for the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • NK cells → direct tumor-cell killing

  • Macrophages → tumor cell destruction

  • ADCC → antibody-coated tumor cells → immune-cell killing

  • Helper T cells → mainly immune regulation/coordination

Exam Pearl:
Key anti-tumor effectors: NK cells, macrophages, and CTLs; ADCC is an important mechanism.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) Which of the following is a cause of Secondary haemorrhage?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Secondary haemorrhage occurs after the initial bleeding has stopped, usually due to infection, sloughing of a vessel wall, or pressure necrosis of the vessel. Pressure necrosis gradually erodes the vessel wall and can cause delayed bleeding. Slippage of a ligature and dislodgement of a clot are classically causes of reactionary haemorrhage, which occurs within the first 24 hours after surgery. Normalisation of blood pressure is not a typical cause.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary haemorrhage → at the time of injury/operation

  • Reactionary haemorrhage → within ~24 hours

  • Secondary haemorrhage → usually 7–14 days later

  • Secondary causes → infection + pressure necrosis

  • Ligature slippage → reactionary haemorrhage

Exam Pearl:
Secondary haemorrhage = infection → vessel wall erosion/pressure necrosis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) Which one is correct regarding autoclaving process of sterilization?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Autoclaving is a method of sterilization using moist heat under pressure. The standard condition is approximately 121°C at 15 psi pressure for 15 minutes. This is sufficient to destroy vegetative bacteria, viruses, fungi, and bacterial spores. The exact time can vary depending on the load, volume, and type of material, but 121°C for 15 minutes is the classic exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Autoclave → moist heat

  • Standard → 121°C + 15 psi + 15 min

  • Kills → bacterial spores

  • Principle → steam under pressure

Exam Pearl:
Autoclave = 121°C for 15 minutes at 15 psi.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) Which one is the most important diagnostic method in enteric fever?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Blood culture is the most important and preferred diagnostic test for enteric (typhoid) fever, particularly during the first week of illness when bacteremia is prominent. It can directly identify Salmonella Typhi or S. Paratyphi and allows antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The Widal test has limited sensitivity and specificity and is less reliable, especially in endemic areas. Urine culture may occasionally be positive, while CBC findings are nonspecific.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Enteric fever → Blood culture

  • Best yield → 1st week

  • Widal → limited specificity/sensitivity

  • CBC → nonspecific

  • Organism → Salmonella Typhi / Paratyphi

Exam Pearl:
Suspected enteric fever → take blood culture before antibiotics whenever possible.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) Visceral leishmaniasis is the result of which parasitic manifestation?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is caused primarily by the Leishmania donovani complex, especially L. donovani and L. infantum. The parasite infects cells of the reticuloendothelial system, particularly macrophages in the spleen, liver, bone marrow, and lymph nodes. Typical features include prolonged fever, massive splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, pancytopenia, and weight loss.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Visceral leishmaniasis → L. donovani

  • Also called → Kala-azar

  • Vector → Sandfly (Phlebotomus)

  • Main sites → spleen, liver, bone marrow

  • L. tropica → mainly cutaneous leishmaniasis

Exam Pearl:
“Donovani → visceral (kala-azar); Tropica → cutaneous.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) Which one is normal haemoglobin?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the given options, Hb-F (fetal hemoglobin) is the normal hemoglobin found predominantly in the fetus and newborn. It consists of 2 alpha (α) and 2 gamma (γ) chains (α₂γ₂). In healthy adults, Hb-A (α₂β₂) is the predominant normal hemoglobin, but Hb-A is not included in the options. Hb-S, Hb-C, and Hb-E are abnormal hemoglobin variants.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hb-A → normal adult Hb

  • Hb-F → normal fetal Hb

  • Hb-S → sickle cell disease

  • Hb-C → Hb variant causing HbC disease

  • Hb-E → structural variant/β-thalassemia association

Exam Pearl:
Adult = Hb-A; fetus = Hb-F.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) Which of the following test doesn't correspond to diagnosis of hemophilia?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) and hemophilia B (factor IX deficiency) are disorders of the intrinsic coagulation pathway. Therefore, APTT is prolonged, while PT remains normal. Bleeding time (BT) is usually normal because platelet function is unaffected. Clotting time (CT) may be prolonged. Hence, a normal APTT does not correspond to hemophilia and is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hemophilia → ↑ APTT

  • PT → Normal

  • BT → Normal

  • Factor VIII → Hemophilia A

  • Factor IX → Hemophilia B

Exam Pearl:
Hemophilia = prolonged APTT with normal PT and BT.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) Full recovery occurs in .... % of adults following acute HBV infection?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In adults with acute hepatitis B (HBV) infection, approximately 90–95% achieve spontaneous recovery and develop protective immunity. Only about 5–10% of adults progress to chronic HBV infection. The risk of chronicity is much higher when infection occurs in infancy or early childhood.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adult acute HBV → 90–95% recover

  • Adults developing chronic infection → ~5–10%

  • Infants infected perinatally → ~90% become chronic

  • Chronic HBV → increased risk of cirrhosis + hepatocellular carcinoma

Exam Pearl:
Adult HBV: ~95% recover, ~5% become chronic.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) Which one is the most common organism for UTI?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Escherichia coli is the most common causative organism of urinary tract infection (UTI), accounting for the majority of community-acquired UTIs. It is a Gram-negative bacillus from the intestinal flora and commonly causes cystitis and pyelonephritis. Staphylococcus saprophyticus is an important cause of UTI, especially in young sexually active women, but is less common than E. coli. Pseudomonas and Proteus are more often associated with complicated or healthcare-associated UTIs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common UTI organism → E. coli

  • Gram-negative bacillus

  • Important virulence factor → P-fimbriae

  • S. saprophyticus → young sexually active women

  • Proteus → urease positive, associated with struvite stones

Exam Pearl:
UTI → think E. coli first.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) Which is not true about Nephrotic syndrome?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option1: Positive history of pharyngitis or skin infection
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A history of recent pharyngitis or skin infection is classically associated with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (PSGN), which typically presents as a nephritic syndrome, not nephrotic syndrome. Nephrotic syndrome is characterized by massive proteinuria (>3.5 g/day in adults), hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia. In many common causes, particularly minimal change disease, C3 is usually normal, and relapses are common, especially in children.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nephrotic syndrome → massive proteinuria

  • → hypoalbuminemia + edema + hyperlipidemia

  • C3 → usually normal

  • Relapse → common, especially in children with minimal change disease

  • Recent sore throat/skin infection → think PSGN (nephritic)

Exam Pearl:
Recent streptococcal infection + low C3 + hematuria → PSGN, not classic nephrotic syndrome.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Peptostreptococcus can be treated with.....
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Peptostreptococcus is an anaerobic Gram-positive cocci that is generally susceptible to penicillin, making Penicillin G a classic treatment choice. These organisms are part of the normal flora of the oral cavity, gastrointestinal tract, and female genital tract and can cause polymicrobial anaerobic infections, including abscesses. In clinical practice, antibiotic selection depends on the site of infection and susceptibility patterns, and broader anaerobic coverage may be needed for polymicrobial infections.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Peptostreptococcus → anaerobic Gram-positive cocci

  • Classic susceptible drug → Penicillin G

  • Commonly involved in → abscesses and polymicrobial infections

  • Severe anaerobic infections → may require broader anaerobic coverage

Exam Pearl:
Peptostreptococcus → Penicillin G (classic exam answer).

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) What type of spore is produced by C. Tetani?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Clostridium tetani produces a terminal spore, which gives the bacterium its characteristic “drumstick” or “tennis-racket” appearance. The spore is located at the end of the bacillus and causes the swollen terminal end. C. tetani is an anaerobic, Gram-positive, spore-forming bacillus that produces tetanospasmin, the neurotoxin responsible for tetanus.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • C. tetani → Terminal spore

  • Appearance → Drumstick/tennis racket

  • Toxin → Tetanospasmin

  • Disease → Tetanus

  • Anaerobic Gram-positive bacillus

Exam Pearl:
C. tetani = terminal spore = drumstick appearance.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) HSV-2 leads to latent infection in which ganglia?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
HSV-2 primarily causes genital herpes and establishes latent infection in the sacral sensory ganglia, especially the sacral dorsal root ganglia. The virus travels along sensory nerves from the genital mucosa to these ganglia, where it remains latent and can later reactivate, producing recurrent genital lesions. In contrast, HSV-1 classically establishes latency in the trigeminal ganglion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HSV-1 → Trigeminal ganglion

  • HSV-2 → Sacral ganglia

  • HSV-1 → commonly orolabial lesions

  • HSV-2 → commonly genital herpes

  • Reactivation → recurrent vesicular lesions

Exam Pearl:
“HSV-1 = Trigeminal; HSV-2 = Sacral.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) Which is not a cardinal features of Hansen's disease?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option3: Acid fast bacilli on skin smears
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The cardinal features of Hansen’s disease (leprosy) are clinical/diagnostic findings: (1) definite loss of sensation in a skin lesion, (2) thickened peripheral nerve with sensory or motor deficit, and (3) demonstration of acid-fast bacilli in a slit-skin smear. Mycobacterium leprae is indeed the causative organism, but “caused by M. leprae” is not itself a cardinal clinical/diagnostic feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cardinal feature → anaesthetic skin lesion

  • → thickened peripheral nerve + deficit

  • → AFB in slit-skin smear

  • Causative organism → M. leprae

Exam Pearl:
Leprosy cardinal signs = sensory loss + nerve thickening + AFB.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) Which organ is mostly affected in PUD?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The first part of the duodenum (duodenal bulb) is the most common site affected by peptic ulcer disease (PUD). Duodenal ulcers are commonly located in the anterior or posterior wall of the duodenal bulb. The stomach is another important site, but duodenal ulcers are classically more common. Ulcers in the second part of the duodenum are much less common.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common site of PUD → 1st part of duodenum

  • Gastric ulcer → commonly along lesser curvature

  • Posterior duodenal ulcer → risk of gastroduodenal artery bleeding

  • Anterior duodenal ulcer → risk of perforation

Exam Pearl:
PUD → most commonly affects the duodenal bulb (1st part of duodenum).

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) Amoebic liver abscess is caused by.......?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
An amoebic liver abscess is caused by Entamoeba histolytica, an intestinal protozoan parasite. The trophozoites invade the colonic mucosa and can enter the portal circulation, reaching the liver and causing an abscess. Patients commonly present with fever, right upper quadrant pain, and hepatomegaly. The abscess classically contains thick brown material often described as “anchovy sauce/paste.”

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Amoebic liver abscess → Entamoeba histolytica

  • Route → portal circulation from colon → liver

  • Common symptom → fever + RUQ pain

  • Aspirate → “anchovy sauce”

Exam Pearl:
Amoebic liver abscess = E. histolytica.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) Which is not true about RBC?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A normal RBC is biconcave, anucleate, and approximately 7–8 µm in diameter. Its thickness is about 2–2.5 µm at the peripheral rim and around 1 µm centrally. RBCs are relatively fragile cells, especially when exposed to osmotic stress, although their flexible membrane allows them to pass through narrow capillaries. Therefore, “non-fragile” is the incorrect statement.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RBC → biconcave

  • Mature RBC → no nucleus

  • Diameter → ~7–8 µm

  • Thickness → ~2–2.5 µm at edge

  • Lifespan → ~120 days

Exam Pearl:
RBC = biconcave + anucleate + flexible, not “non-fragile.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) ECG change in hypokalemia is all except which of the following?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The classic ECG changes of hypokalemia include flattened or inverted T waves, ST-segment depression, and prominent U waves. The QU interval may appear prolonged because the prominent U wave merges with the T wave. Strictly speaking, the QT interval itself is usually normal, so “prolonged QT interval” is the best answer for the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypokalemia → ↓/flattened T wave

  • → ST depression

  • → Prominent U wave

  • → Apparent QU prolongation

  • Hyperkalemia → peaked T waves, widened QRS

Exam Pearl:
Hypokalemia = ST depression + flat T + prominent U waves.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) What will be the type of hypoxia in CO poisoning?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning causes anemic hypoxia because CO binds to hemoglobin with an affinity about 200–250 times greater than oxygen, forming carboxyhemoglobin (COHb). This reduces the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and also shifts the remaining oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the left, impairing oxygen unloading to tissues. Therefore, despite a potentially normal arterial PO2PO2​​, tissue oxygen delivery is impaired.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CO poisoning → Anemic hypoxia

  • CO + Hb → Carboxyhemoglobin

  • CO affinity for Hb → ~200–250× O₂

  • PaO₂ → may remain normal

  • Oxygen content → decreased

Exam Pearl:
CO poisoning = anemic hypoxia due to carboxyhemoglobin.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) Most of the CO2 carried in the blood in the form of___?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Most of the CO₂ in blood (~70%) is transported as bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻). Inside RBCs, carbon dioxide combines with water under the action of carbonic anhydrase to form carbonic acid, which dissociates into H⁺ and HCO₃⁻. About 20–23% is transported as carbamino compounds, mainly carbaminohemoglobin, while approximately 7–10% is physically dissolved in plasma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ~70% → HCO₃⁻

  • ~20–23% → Carbamino compounds

  • ~7–10% → Dissolved CO₂

  • Key enzyme → Carbonic anhydrase

Exam Pearl:
CO₂ transport: bicarbonate > carbaminohemoglobin > dissolved CO₂.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) Gastric emptying is inhibited by which of the following?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
CCK-PZ (cholecystokinin-pancreozymin) inhibits gastric emptying and slows gastric motility. It is released from I cells of the duodenum and jejunum in response to fatty acids and amino acids. This delay allows adequate time for digestion and absorption of nutrients in the small intestine. Secretin also inhibits gastric emptying and acid secretion, but among these options, CCK-PZ is the classic and strongest answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CCK-PZ → inhibits gastric emptying

  • Released from → I cells

  • Stimulus → fats + amino acids

  • Main actions → gallbladder contraction + pancreatic enzyme secretion

  • Secretin → ↓ gastric acid secretion and motility

Exam Pearl:
Fat in the duodenum → CCK → slows gastric emptying.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) Which is true about blood flow of nephron?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Approximately 90–95% of renal blood flow goes to the renal cortex, while only about 5–10% reaches the medulla. The cortex receives most of the blood because it contains the glomeruli, where filtration occurs. The renal medulla has relatively low blood flow to maintain the osmotic gradient necessary for urine concentration.

Among the given options, “about 98% in cortex” is the closest and intended answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Renal blood flow → predominantly cortex

  • Cortex → ~90–95%

  • Medulla → ~5–10%

  • Glomeruli → located in cortex

  • Low medullary blood flow → helps preserve medullary osmotic gradient

Exam Pearl:
Most renal blood flow goes to the cortex, not the medulla.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Which endocrine gland acts without pituitary control?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The parathyroid glands function largely independently of pituitary control. Their main regulator is the serum ionized calcium concentration. When blood calcium falls, parathyroid chief cells release parathyroid hormone (PTH), which increases serum calcium through effects on bone, kidneys, and indirectly the intestine via activation of vitamin D. In contrast, the thyroid, adrenal cortex, and ovaries are primarily regulated through the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Parathyroid → regulated by serum Ca²⁺

  • Thyroid → TSH

  • Adrenal cortex → ACTH (except aldosterone, mainly regulated by RAAS/K⁺)

  • Ovary → FSH/LH

Exam Pearl:
Endocrine gland independent of pituitary control → Parathyroid.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) In which condition frog like husky voice is found?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A frog-like, husky, or hoarse voice is a classic feature of myxoedema, which results from severe hypothyroidism. Accumulation of mucopolysaccharides in the tissues, including around the vocal cords, causes edema and produces a deep, hoarse, husky voice. Other features include dry skin, facial puffiness, cold intolerance, constipation, bradycardia, and lethargy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Myxoedema → husky/hoarse voice

  • Cause → severe hypothyroidism

  • Mechanism → mucopolysaccharide deposition + edema

  • Other features → dry skin, puffiness, cold intolerance, bradycardia

Exam Pearl:
Husky/frog-like voice + hypothyroidism → Myxoedema.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) Sex hormones are secreted from which part of adrenal gland?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The zona reticularis, the innermost layer of the adrenal cortex, primarily produces adrenal androgens, which are sex steroid hormones such as DHEA and androstenedione. The adrenal cortex has three layers, remembered by GFR:

  • Zona Glomerulosa → Mineralocorticoids (aldosterone)

  • Zona Fasciculata → Glucocorticoids (cortisol)

  • Zona Reticularis → Androgens

The adrenal medulla produces catecholamines such as adrenaline and noradrenaline.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • G → Glomerulosa → Mineralocorticoids

  • F → Fasciculata → Glucocorticoids

  • R → Reticularis → Androgens

Exam Pearl:
“GFR = Salt, Sugar, Sex” → Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Which one is an acute complication of DM?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is an acute, life-threatening complication of diabetes mellitus, most commonly associated with type 1 DM. It results from severe insulin deficiency, causing hyperglycemia, increased lipolysis, ketone production, and metabolic acidosis. Retinopathy and nephropathy are chronic microvascular complications, while stroke is generally considered a chronic macrovascular complication associated with diabetes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • DKA → acute complication

  • Commonly → Type 1 DM

  • Triad → hyperglycemia + ketosis + metabolic acidosis

  • Retinopathy → chronic microvascular

  • Nephropathy → chronic microvascular

  • Stroke → chronic macrovascular complication

Exam Pearl:
Acute DM complications → DKA and HHS.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) Which one has longest half-life?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thyroxine (T4) has the longest half-life among the options, approximately 7 days. This long half-life is mainly due to its high protein binding in plasma, particularly to thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG). In comparison, PTH, insulin, and glucagon have much shorter half-lives, generally measured in minutes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T4 → half-life ~7 days

  • T3 → ~1 day

  • PTH → ~4 minutes

  • Insulin → ~5–6 minutes

  • Glucagon → ~5–10 minutes

Exam Pearl:
Longest half-life among these hormones = Thyroxine (T4).

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) The part of cell body from which axon arises is called....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The axon hillock is the specialized region of the cell body (soma) from which the axon originates. It is also an important site for action potential initiation because it contains a high density of voltage-gated sodium channels, particularly in the adjacent initial segment.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Axon arises from → Axon hillock

  • Node of Ranvier → gap between myelin segments

  • Boutons terminaux → axon terminals

  • Synaptic cleft → space between pre- and postsynaptic neurons

Exam Pearl:
Cell body → axon hillock → axon.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) Which reflex causes flexion of forearm?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The biceps jerk (biceps reflex) produces flexion of the forearm at the elbow. It is a deep tendon reflex mediated mainly by the musculocutaneous nerve and C5–C6 spinal nerve roots, predominantly C5. Tapping the biceps tendon stretches the biceps muscle, causing reflex contraction and elbow flexion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Biceps jerk → forearm flexion

  • Nerve → Musculocutaneous nerve

  • Roots → C5–C6

  • Triceps jerk → forearm extension

  • Supinator (brachioradialis) jerk → elbow flexion + forearm movement

Exam Pearl:
Biceps = flexion; Triceps = extension.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) Which acts as final relay station for sensory stimuli?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The thalamus is the major relay station for sensory information to the cerebral cortex. Almost all sensory pathways, except olfaction, relay through the thalamus before reaching the cerebral cortex. Different thalamic nuclei relay different sensory modalities—for example, the VPL relays body sensation, while the VPM relays facial sensation and taste.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thalamus → major sensory relay station

  • VPL → body sensation

  • VPM → face sensation + taste

  • Lateral geniculate body → vision

  • Medial geniculate body → hearing

  • Olfaction → exception (does not initially relay through thalamus)

Exam Pearl:
Thalamus = gateway/relay station to the cerebral cortex.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) What is the structural & functional unit of nervous system?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. It is specialized to receive, process, and transmit nerve impulses. A typical neuron consists of a cell body (soma), dendrites, and an axon. Dendrites mainly receive signals, while the axon conducts impulses away from the cell body.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Structural & functional unit → Neuron

  • Dendrites → receive signals

  • Cell body → metabolic/control center

  • Axon → conducts impulses away from soma

  • Nephron → structural & functional unit of kidney

Exam Pearl:
Nervous system → Neuron; Kidney → Nephron.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) What is the cause of Anisometropia?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option1: Increase in anteroposterior diameter of the eyeball
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Decrease in anteroposterior diameter of the eyeball
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).option3: Difference in refractive power of both eyes
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Anisometropia means a difference in refractive error/power between the two eyes. The difference may result from unequal axial length or unequal refractive power of the cornea/lens, but the defining feature is that the two eyes have different refractive powers. Significant anisometropia can cause unequal retinal image sizes (aniseikonia) and, particularly in children, may lead to amblyopia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anisometropia → unequal refractive power between two eyes

  • Myopia → increased axial length

  • Hypermetropia → decreased axial length

  • Presbyopia → loss of lens elasticity

Exam Pearl:
Anisometropia = unequal refraction between the two eyes.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Which Epithelial cell junction is devoid of any Cytoskeletal components?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the given epithelial cell junctions, the gap junction is classically considered to be devoid of cytoskeletal attachment. Gap junctions are formed by connexin proteins that assemble into connexons, creating channels between adjacent cells for the passage of ions and small molecules. In contrast, adherens junctions and desmosomes are linked to actin and intermediate filaments, respectively. Tight junctions are also associated with the actin cytoskeleton through ZO proteins, so they are not devoid of cytoskeletal components.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tight junction → Actin

  • Adherens junction → Actin

  • Desmosome → Intermediate filaments

  • Gap junction → No cytoskeletal attachment

  • Gap junction proteins → Connexins

Exam Pearl:
Gap junction = intercellular communication, not mechanical anchoring.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) What is the lining epithelium of vagina?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The vagina is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium. This epithelium provides protection against mechanical abrasion while maintaining a moist surface. Unlike the skin, it does not have a keratinized surface layer. The vaginal mucosa also contains glycogen-rich epithelial cells, which contribute to an acidic vaginal environment through lactobacilli.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Vagina → Non-keratinized stratified squamous

  • Skin → Keratinized stratified squamous

  • Urinary bladder → Transitional epithelium

  • Alveoli → Simple squamous

Exam Pearl:
Vagina = non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) What is the location of conducting system of heart?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The conducting system of the heart is primarily located in the subendocardial layer, particularly the Purkinje fibers, which lie beneath the endocardium and rapidly distribute electrical impulses through the ventricular myocardium. The SA node and AV node are located in specialized areas of the atrial myocardium, but the terminal conducting network is characteristically subendocardial.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Purkinje fibers → Subendocardial layer

  • SA node → right atrium near SVC

  • AV node → interatrial septum near coronary sinus

  • Bundle of His → membranous interventricular septum

Exam Pearl:
Purkinje fibers = subendocardial conducting network.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) Which layer in an artery is primarily smooth muscle?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The tunica media is the middle layer of an artery and is composed predominantly of smooth muscle cells, along with elastic fibers. Its contraction and relaxation regulate vascular tone, blood pressure, and blood flow. The tunica intima mainly consists of endothelium, while the tunica externa (adventitia) is mainly connective tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tunica intima → Endothelium

  • Tunica media → Smooth muscle ⭐

  • Tunica externa → Connective tissue

  • Arteries generally have a thicker tunica media than veins.

Exam Pearl:
“Media = Muscle.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) What is the function of vestibulocerebellar tract?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The vestibulocerebellar tract is mainly concerned with equilibrium and coordination of eye movements. It carries information from the vestibular apparatus to the flocculonodular lobe of the cerebellum, which helps maintain balance and coordinate eye movements with head movements. Therefore, among the given options, movements of eyeballs is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Vestibulocerebellum → balance + eye movements

  • Main lobe → Flocculonodular lobe

  • Input → Vestibular apparatus

  • Function → Equilibrium and coordination of eye movements

Exam Pearl:
Vestibulocerebellar tract = balance + eye movements.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) Endolymph has large quantity of.......?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Endolymph is the fluid present within the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear. It has a high concentration of potassium (K⁺) and a low concentration of sodium (Na⁺), resembling the intracellular fluid. In contrast, perilymph is rich in sodium and relatively low in potassium, resembling extracellular fluid. The high K⁺ concentration of endolymph is essential for generating the electrical potential required for hearing and balance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Endolymph → high K⁺, low Na⁺

  • Perilymph → high Na⁺, low K⁺

  • Endolymph → membranous labyrinth

  • Perilymph → bony labyrinth

  • Important for → hearing + equilibrium

Exam Pearl:
“Endolymph = K⁺ rich; Perilymph = Na⁺ rich.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) What is the root value of Cremasteric reflex?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The cremasteric reflex is elicited by stroking the upper medial thigh, producing elevation of the ipsilateral testis through contraction of the cremaster muscle. Its spinal cord root value is L1–L2, with L1 being particularly important. The afferent limb is carried mainly by the ilioinguinal nerve, while the efferent limb is via the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cremasteric reflex → L1–L2

  • Afferent → Ilioinguinal nerve

  • Efferent → Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve

  • Response → Elevation of testis

Exam Pearl:
Cremasteric reflex = L1–L2.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Which of the following structure is composed of actin subunits and allow motility and most contractile activity in cells?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Microfilaments are composed primarily of actin subunits. They are responsible for cell motility, muscle contraction, cytokinesis, and changes in cell shape. Actin interacts with myosin to produce most forms of cellular contractile activity. Microtubules are made of tubulin, while intermediate filaments are composed of proteins such as keratin, vimentin, and desmin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Microfilament → Actin → motility & contraction

  • Microtubule → Tubulin → intracellular transport, mitotic spindle

  • Intermediate filament → Keratin/vimentin/desmin → structural strength

  • Actin + myosin → muscle contraction

Exam Pearl:
Actin = Microfilament = Motility + Contractility.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) Which of the following degrades denatured or otherwise nonfunctional polypeptides?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Proteasomes degrade denatured, damaged, misfolded, or otherwise nonfunctional intracellular proteins. Many proteins are first tagged with ubiquitin, which directs them to the 26S proteasome for degradation into small peptides. This is an important part of cellular protein quality control.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Proteasome → degrades damaged/misfolded intracellular proteins

  • Ubiquitin → tags proteins for degradation

  • Ribosome → protein synthesis

  • Lysosome → degrades material delivered to lysosomes, including macromolecules and organelles

  • Peroxisome → fatty acid oxidation + H₂O₂ metabolism

Exam Pearl:
Ubiquitin + Proteasome = intracellular protein degradation.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) Which is the longest part of cell cycle?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the phases listed, G1 phase is generally the longest phase of the cell cycle in actively dividing cells. During G1, the cell grows, synthesizes proteins and RNA, and prepares for DNA replication. The S phase is devoted to DNA replication, while G2 involves preparation for mitosis. G0 is a quiescent/resting state and is not considered a phase of the active cell cycle.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • G1 → longest phase ⭐

  • S → DNA synthesis/replication

  • G2 → preparation for mitosis

  • M → mitosis + cytokinesis

  • G0 → resting/quiescent state

Exam Pearl:
Active cell cycle → G1 is usually the longest phase.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) Which of the following is not a criteria of mitosis cell division?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
During mitosis, chromosomes become clearly visible because chromatin condenses, beginning in prophase. Therefore, saying “chromosomes are not visible” is not a criterion of mitosis. Mitosis occurs mainly in somatic cells, and compared with meiosis, it has a relatively short prophase and usually a shorter overall division process.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Mitosis → somatic cells

  • Chromosomes → visible/condensed

  • Prophase → relatively short

  • Produces → 2 genetically similar diploid cells

  • No crossing over → mitosis

Exam Pearl:
Chromosomes become visible during prophase of mitosis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) Which is the most superficial layer of epidermis of skin?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The stratum corneum is the most superficial layer of the epidermis. It consists mainly of dead, flattened, keratin-filled cells called corneocytes, which provide a protective barrier against mechanical injury, pathogens, and water loss.

The epidermal layers from deep → superficial are:

Stratum basale → Stratum spinosum → Stratum granulosum → Stratum lucidum → Stratum corneum

Stratum lucidum is present only in thick skin (palms and soles).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most superficial → Stratum corneum

  • Deepest → Stratum basale

  • Lucidum → only thick skin

  • Corneum → dead, keratinized cells

Exam Pearl:
“Corneum = Cornified outermost layer.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) Transitional area where the transparent cornea merges with the opaque sclera is called......?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The limbus (corneal limbus) is the transitional zone where the transparent cornea meets the opaque sclera. It is clinically important because the trabecular meshwork and Canal of Schlemm are located near this region and participate in aqueous humor drainage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cornea + sclera junction → Limbus

  • Trabecular meshwork → drains aqueous humor

  • Canal of Schlemm → aqueous drainage channel

  • Uvea → iris + ciliary body + choroid

Exam Pearl:
Transparent cornea → opaque sclera = corneal limbus.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) What is the lining epithelium of the outer pigmented layer of retina?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The outer pigmented layer of the retina is the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), which is composed of simple cuboidal epithelial cells. These cells contain melanin and perform important functions such as phagocytosis of shed photoreceptor outer segments, vitamin A metabolism, and absorption of excess light.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Retinal pigment epithelium → Simple cuboidal

  • Contains → Melanin

  • Function → absorbs light + supports photoreceptors

  • Retina → neural layer + pigmented layer

Exam Pearl:
RPE = simple cuboidal epithelium.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) The nervous system develops from which germ layer?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The nervous system develops from the ectoderm, specifically through the process of neurulation. The ectoderm forms the neural plate, which folds to form the neural tube. The neural tube gives rise to the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), while the neural crest contributes to much of the peripheral nervous system.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nervous system → Ectoderm

  • Neural plate → neural tube

  • Neural tube → brain + spinal cord

  • Neural crest → much of PNS

  • Mesoderm → muscle, bone, connective tissue

  • Endoderm → GI and respiratory epithelium

Exam Pearl:
Ectoderm = nervous system + epidermis.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) The Tympanic membrane is connected to.....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The tympanic membrane (eardrum) is directly attached to the handle (manubrium) of the malleus, the first of the three auditory ossicles. Vibrations of the tympanic membrane are transmitted through the malleus → incus → stapes, ultimately reaching the oval window of the inner ear.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tympanic membrane → Malleus

  • Ossicles → Malleus → Incus → Stapes

  • Malleus → attached to tympanic membrane

  • Stapes → footplate attached to oval window

Exam Pearl:
“TM → Malleus → Incus → Stapes → Oval window.”

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬) Which type of neurons are the most common?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Multipolar neurons are the most common type of neuron in the nervous system. They have one axon and multiple dendrites, making them well suited for integrating information from many inputs. They are found predominantly in the central nervous system, including motor neurons and many interneurons.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common → Multipolar neurons

  • Structure → 1 axon + multiple dendrites

  • Common examples → motor neurons, interneurons

  • Pseudounipolar → sensory neurons of dorsal root ganglia

  • Bipolar → retina, olfactory pathways, vestibulocochlear system

Exam Pearl:
Multipolar = most numerous + most common neuronal type.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) Schwann cell corresponds to which cell in CNS?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Schwann cells are the myelinating glial cells of the peripheral nervous system (PNS). Their functional counterpart in the central nervous system (CNS) is the oligodendrocyte, which forms myelin around CNS axons.

One oligodendrocyte can myelinate multiple axons/segments, whereas one Schwann cell generally myelinates one segment of one axon.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PNS myelin → Schwann cell

  • CNS myelin → Oligodendrocyte ⭐

  • Astrocyte → support + blood-brain barrier

  • Microglia → phagocytic immune cells

  • Ependymal cells → line ventricles and central canal

Exam Pearl:
Schwann = PNS; Oligodendrocyte = CNS.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) What is the Sensory Receptor of cochlea?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The spiral organ (Organ of Corti) is the sensory receptor organ of the cochlea and is responsible for hearing. It is located on the basilar membrane within the cochlear duct. Its sensory hair cells convert mechanical vibrations caused by sound into electrical nerve signals transmitted through the cochlear division of CN VIII.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cochlea → Spiral organ (Organ of Corti) → hearing

  • Utricle/saccule → Maculae → linear acceleration & gravity

  • Semicircular ducts → Cristae ampullares → angular acceleration

  • CN VIII → Vestibulocochlear nerve

Exam Pearl:
Cochlea → Organ of Corti; Semicircular canals → Cristae; Utricle/Saccule → Maculae.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) The part of the nerve fibre between two nodes of Ranvier is called the.....?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The internode is the portion of a myelinated nerve fiber between two consecutive nodes of Ranvier. It is covered by a segment of the myelin sheath formed by Schwann cells in the PNS or oligodendrocytes in the CNS. The nodes of Ranvier are gaps in the myelin sheath where voltage-gated ion channels are concentrated, allowing saltatory conduction of the action potential.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Between two nodes → Internode

  • Node of Ranvier → gap in myelin sheath

  • Myelin → increases conduction velocity

  • Saltatory conduction → impulse “jumps” from node to node

Exam Pearl:
Node → Internode → Node = one myelinated segment.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) How many C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage are there in trachea?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The trachea contains approximately 16–20 C-shaped rings of hyaline cartilage in standard anatomical descriptions. These incomplete rings maintain airway patency while allowing the posterior membranous wall to accommodate the esophagus during swallowing.

 Note: The provided options are inconsistent with the commonly accepted value. If your source specifically expects one of these options, গ) 16–20 is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tracheal cartilage → C-shaped hyaline cartilage

  • Commonly → 16–20 rings

  • Posterior gap → trachealis muscle

  • Function → keeps airway open while permitting esophageal expansion

Exam Pearl:
Trachea = ~16–20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) What is the location of epiglottis?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped structure made of elastic cartilage located at the entrance of the larynx. During swallowing, it folds backward to help prevent food and liquid from entering the airway.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Epiglottis → Larynx

  • Type of cartilage → Elastic cartilage

  • Function → protects airway during swallowing

  • It lies behind the tongue and in front of the laryngeal inlet

Exam Pearl:
Epiglottis = elastic cartilage at the laryngeal inlet.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) Which is true about ileum?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The ileum has characteristic anatomical and histological features that distinguish it from the jejunum. Its mesentery contains less fat near the intestinal wall, but the classic distinction is that jejunal mesentery has fewer arcades and larger “windows,” whereas ileal mesentery has more arcades and smaller windows. Ileum also has numerous Peyer’s patches, shorter and fewer villi, and more goblet cells. Therefore, among the given options, “window absent in mesentery” is the best answer, although the wording is somewhat simplified.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ileum → numerous Peyer’s patches

  • Villi → short, broad, finger-like

  • Mesentery → more fat + more arterial arcades

  • Jejunum → fewer arcades + larger mesenteric windows

  • Ileum → more lymphoid tissue

Exam Pearl:
Jejunum = large mesenteric windows; Ileum = small/less obvious windows.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) Which one is internal genital organ?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The vagina is an internal female genital organ. It is a muscular, fibromuscular canal extending from the cervix to the vaginal opening.

The other options are external genital structures:

  • Labia minora → external genitalia

  • Vestibule → part of the vulva

  • Clitoris → external genital organ

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Internal genital organs → Ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus, vagina

  • External genitalia (vulva) → Labia, clitoris, vestibule, mons pubis

  • Vagina → connects cervix to exterior

Exam Pearl:
Vagina is the only internal genital organ among these options.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Which one is the Normal position of uterus?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The normal position of the uterus is anteverted and anteflexed. However, when only one option is provided from the given choices, anteversion is generally accepted as the best answer.

  • Anteversion → uterus tilted forward relative to the vagina.

  • Anteflexion → body of uterus bent forward relative to the cervix.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Normal uterus → Anteverted + anteflexed

  • Anteversion → uterus–vagina relationship

  • Anteflexion → body–cervix relationship

  • Retroversion/retroflexion → backward position

Exam Pearl:
Normal uterine position = anteverted + anteflexed.

Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) Which of the following is adult derivative of notochord?
Final Model Test-09 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
